policy: A new versioned record. The frozen CE-00.1 input tests/core-evolution/scope-decisions.v1.json is not edited.
Each closure names the decision, the lot that closes it, the closing decision, its rationale, the evidence paths and the commands that executed it. A split decision names the part each lot owns.
A closure is a contract statement, not a support claim: browser support claims attach to emitted CSS and exact target evidence only (docs/architecture/ce-01.1-browser-targets.md).
One register across lots: a later lot closes an earlier deferral in place and keeps the superseded text under `supersedes` (task, status, closesIn, decision); it never deletes a closure.

closures.decision: pandamstyle:default@1 is the Browserslist query 'chrome >= 120, edge >= 120, firefox >= 121, and_chr >= 120, and_ff >= 121, safari >= 18.2, ios_saf >= 18.2', resolved with browserslist 4.28.0, caniuse-lite 1.0.30001799, electron-to-chromium 1.5.459 and baseline-browser-mapping 2.11.23 (exact pins), evaluated on the CE-00.1 BCD 8.1.6 data restricted to emittable paths.
closures.rationale: Floors are measured, not copied: for each default engine, the maximum over the CE-00.2 corpus, the compiler's output for the frozen workloads and its intrinsic emission of the earliest release whose outcome is native or equivalent-fallback. A feature never acceptable on some default engine sets no floor and is listed as a non-binding exception. Orchestrator decision of 2026-10-19.

closures.decision: safari_ios is announced in pandamstyle:default@1 and in the opt-in pandamstyle:ios-safari@1 at floor 18.2, evaluated only on safari_ios statements. The basis is compat-data until #81 records executed evidence. The evidence schema refuses Playwright WebKit and other WebKit ports as safari or safari_ios evidence, refuses desktop and headless runs as safari_ios evidence, and labels Apple iOS Simulator evidence executed-simulator, distinct from a real device (executed).
closures.rationale: No dependency range or Playwright engine implies Safari/iOS support (#44 deliverable 8). Compat data is never a qualification.

closures.decision: pandamstyle:electron@1 is the query 'electron 44.7' with platform electron, mapped by the pinned electron-to-chromium to Chromium 152 (basis derived-from-electron). platform:electron/* keys are incompatible (platform-scoped) on every profile without that platform. On Electron, -webkit-app-region and -webkit-font-smoothing evaluate native; -webkit-user-drag is unknown (no-data) because it is not in the emittable data set until CE-05 admits it.
closures.rationale: Electron is not Chrome: the platform scope keeps desktop-renderer extensions out of web profiles.

closures.decision: Android WebView is not in the default profile. It is the opt-in pandamstyle:android-webview@1, query 'android >= 120', on webview_android statements, explicitly unqualified (basis compat-data).

Internet Explorer, legacy EdgeHTML (< 79), Presto Opera (< 15), Opera Mini and BlackBerry resolve to excluded entries with disposition obsolete and a PMS_INCOMPATIBLE_TARGET_ENGINE warning; a profile with no announced engine is an error. -ms-, -o- and -khtml- properties in emitted CSS are incompatible with reason obsolete-engine on every profile.
closures.rationale: Old target syntax is accepted but promises nothing (LIM-05).

closures.decision: Every D-BP-06 registry entry has a determined per-engine outcome. The two entries emittable today are evaluated on their BCD data: forced-color-adjust is equivalent-fallback (platform-inapplicable) on safari and safari_ios, overscroll-behavior is native under its reviewed partial. The other 33 are not emittable in Alpha 1 and are not in the bundled data (decision 6): a construct naming one is unknown (unrecognized-construct) on every engine and fails closed. Their BCD outcomes are computed when the owning lot admits the property and extends the compat-data inputs.
closures.rationale: The bundled data is restricted to emittable paths (orchestrator decision 6). A non-emittable property cannot reach emitted CSS, and if it did it would never borrow another feature's support.

closures.decision: Prefix emission is a compiler-owned, target-independent rewrite driven by packages/compiler/src/targets/catalog/transforms.v1.json. Version 1 holds one entry: a user-select declaration whose value is auto, text, none or all is preceded, in the same block, by -webkit-user-select with the identical value; every admitted value is paired (Alpha 1 admits none). An entry requires that the variant is, on every announced engine at the O13 floor, an alias of the base (CE-00.1 vendor-legacy-variant), the only form or dropped at parse time; that the admitted values lie in the shared subset; and a committed proof with executed evidence. The outcome of the pair is transformed-with-proof (reason transformation-proven) where the base is not acceptable and the variant's own statements are native: user-select on safari and safari_ios, basis compat-data, executed E4 evidence on Chrome, Safari executed evidence deferred to #81. Prefixed-only or renamed data without an entry stays incompatible; renamed values such as -webkit-fill-available are not aliases.
closures.rationale: The data at the O13 floor and the default profile shows one Alpha 1 admitted value that no Safari release accepts unprefixed and that a semantics-preserving rewrite fixes; every other prefix need is outside Alpha 1 admission and is owned by the lot that admits it.

supersedes.decision: Prefix emission and its identity binding belong to CE-01.2. CE-01.1 keeps prefixed-only data visible as incompatible (prefixed-only); user-select on Safari stays an exception of the default profile until CE-01.2 proves a transformation.
supersedes.rationale: Emission changes CSS bytes and artifact identity.

closures.decision: Value keywords, functions, units, query kinds and descriptors with a BCD statement of their own are their own feature keys (value:<property>/<keyword>, value:<property>/<fn>(), function:<name>[/relative], unit:<unit>, at-rule:<name>/<kind>, descriptor:<at-rule>/<name>), each evaluated on its own path. A keyword without a statement of its own is the property's base grammar.
closures.rationale: #44 AC2: property support is not substituted for keyword or subfeature support.

closures.closesIn: CE-01.1 (data pin); CE-01.2 (transformation engine and identity stage)
closures.decision: CE-01.1 closes the data pin: exact browserslist, caniuse-lite, electron-to-chromium and baseline-browser-mapping runtime dependencies, recorded with version and digest in every resolution record, plus the CE-00.1 BCD 8.1.6 data regenerated byte for byte in CI. CE-01.2 closes the engine: no third-party transformation dependency. The stage is one pure, declaration-local function (applyTransforms) applied in transformRuleEntry to every entry of the complete ordered candidate and to the texts target extraction reads; ordering reads the untransformed text. It runs before styles.css, its source map and the artifact and publication digests, takes no target input (CSS bytes do not depend on targets), and its table digest is recorded as targets.data.transformsDigest. Lightning CSS 1.33.0, PostCSS with Autoprefixer, postcss-preset-env and esbuild were evaluated and rejected (docs/architecture/ce-01.2-transformation-stage.md section 3).
closures.rationale: Option (a) of the accepted CE-01.2 design note: the floors leave one gap a semantics-preserving rewrite closes; a dependency would add a native binary per platform, a second compatibility source and rewrites that change computed values.

supersedes.closesIn: CE-01.1 (data pin); CE-01.2 (transformation engine and identity stage)
supersedes.decision: CE-01.1 closes the data pin: exact browserslist, caniuse-lite, electron-to-chromium and baseline-browser-mapping runtime dependencies, recorded with version and digest in every resolution record, plus the CE-00.1 BCD 8.1.6 data regenerated byte for byte in CI. The transformation engine and its identity stage close in CE-01.2.
supersedes.rationale: The pin binds CE-01.2; emission does not exist yet.

closures.decision: CE-01.1 tracks layers as at-rule:layer/statement and at-rule:layer/block, native-only: useCSSLayers below layer support fails the profile, and the :not(#\#) ladder emitted otherwise is recorded as its own intrinsic feature. CE-01.2: no layer lowering. @layer is native at the O13 minimum on every announced engine. The ladder is an intrinsic ordering mode, not an equivalent: unlayered CSS outside the compiler, !important reversal and revert-layer differ (fixture TX-2). useCSSLayers remains an application-owned ProjectConfig key in SEMANTIC_CONFIG_KEYS; hosts forward it unchanged and never default or rewrite it.
closures.rationale: A lowering changes CSS bytes and cascade semantics.

supersedes.decision: CE-01.1 tracks layers as at-rule:layer/statement and at-rule:layer/block, native-only: useCSSLayers below layer support fails the profile, and the :not(#\#) ladder emitted otherwise is recorded as its own intrinsic feature. Whether a lowering is a proven equivalent, and who owns useCSSLayers, close in CE-01.2.
supersedes.rationale: A lowering changes CSS bytes and cascade semantics.

closures.decision: Media features in emitted conditions get media:<feature> keys (min-/max- folded, range and or syntax separate). The ones the corpus exercises are in the floor set; every one is evaluated per engine and none is assumed equivalent without a reviewed proof. The only reviewed equivalents are the three platform-inapplicable entries.
closures.rationale: Named conditions are emitted verbatim, so their media features are emitted constructs.

closures.decision: A package publishes the computed manifest.json targetRequirements (the required feature keys of its design system's emitted CSS, with the facts digest) and never a target list. The consuming application resolves targets once and evaluates the requirements with evaluateRequirements; package composition calls it in #70.
closures.rationale: Targets are a property of the application.

closures.decision: Impossible cases: no transformation is admitted for light-dark(), @property registration, :has(), container queries (size, style and units), relative colour, color-mix(), the oklch/oklab/lab/lch/color() functions, :dir(), cascade layers or logical properties. Each is native or refused per target, because no build-time rewrite keeps the computed value, inheritance and artifact identity on every engine served by the same bytes. Removing layer wrappers or seeding @property defaults is not a polyfill.
closures.rationale: Derived per feature from the pinned BCD 8.1.6 data at the O13 and default floors, with the executed Lightning CSS probes and fixtures TX-2 to TX-4.

closures.decision: Fallback policy: below support, a required feature is incompatible, an error under enforced targets and a warning under advisory. A design-system author may declare degrade, reported as degraded and never as equivalent. transformed-with-proof comes only from a transform-table entry; equivalent-fallback only from reviewed platform inapplicability, unchanged. alternative-value emission is re-deferred to CE-07.3 (#62): declaration level only, never through a custom property, reported as degraded; until then it is refused with context.deferredTo CE-07.3.

Identity and hosts: the compiler's styles.css bytes are the only input of the canonical digests and of the source map. A host's delivered CSS must be declaration-equivalent to them: the same rules in the same order, per rule the same at-rule conditions, the same selector set (order inside one selector list may differ) and the same declarations in the same order, including every prefixed pair. Whitespace, comments, final semicolons and selector-list order may differ, so minification passes; dropping, adding, merging, reordering or rewriting a declaration is a host redefining targets and fails. One shared normaliser (tools/pms/css-equivalence.cjs, on @csstools/css-tokenizer) is used by the Vite pilot, Rsbuild and Next production qualifications (cssIdentity), with a host targets knob on a repeat build. Hosts' own source maps are the host's concern. The Rsbuild adapter keeps the stylesheet out of builtin:lightningcss-loader and PostCSS and marks the CSS asset that carries it minimized, so neither the loader nor the Lightning CSS minimizer applies the host's browserslist to it.
closures.rationale: Orchestrator answers Q5 and Q6-Q8 of 2026-10-20 (AC3).

orchestratorDecisions.subject: frozen profiles
orchestratorDecisions.decision: pandamstyle:default@1, pandamstyle:ios-safari@1 (ios_saf >= 18.2), pandamstyle:android-webview@1 (android >= 120, opt-in) and pandamstyle:electron@1 (electron 44.7, Chromium 152, platform electron).

orchestratorDecisions.subject: floor method
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Floors from the CE-00.2 corpus, the compiler's output for the frozen workloads and its intrinsic emission; acceptable means native or equivalent-fallback; a feature never acceptable on some default engine sets no floor.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: Wacando text-decoration: underline dotted (W-UTIL-343)
orchestratorDecisions.decision: value:text-decoration/dotted (Safari 26.2) does not set the default floor; under explicit targets it is a correct error on safari and safari_ios (support-after-floor), to be handled as an enhancement in CE-14.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: enforcement
orchestratorDecisions.decision: No targets: advisory, the default profile is still resolved and every outcome recorded, a failing profile is recorded as failing and every target finding is a warning. Explicit targets: enforced, a required incompatible or unknown capability is an error and an author enhancement a warning. Migration note in docs/agent-migration.md.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: Browserslist
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Profiles are Browserslist queries resolved with exact pins and fixed options; clock-dependent and ambient terms are refused; unannounced or obsolete engines are excluded with a warning; a profile with no announced engine is an error.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: compat data
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Only the CE-00.1 BCD 8.1.6, restricted to emittable paths; checks on emitted CSS at keyword and subfeature granularity.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: reviews
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Note reviews keyed by note digest with effectiveFrom; a partial statement is native only under a review with partial: true, missing and a rationale. Reviewed partials: overscroll-behavior, accent-color, and ::marker on Safari limited to color and font-size; font-weight inside ::marker stays an error.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: platform-inapplicable entries
orchestratorDecisions.decision: equivalent-fallback with reason platform-inapplicable for cursor values on safari_ios, forced-color-adjust on safari and safari_ios, and resize on safari_ios and firefox_android.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: unknowns with no BCD entry
orchestratorDecisions.decision: ::-webkit-search-decoration and ::-webkit-outer-spin-button stay unknown, owned by CE-07 (CAP-23) with CE-09 for resets; see unknowns.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: deferrals to CE-01.2 (#45)
orchestratorDecisions.decision: alternative-value emission, D-BP-07 prefix emission, the D-BP-09 transformation engine and the D-BP-10 layer lowering and useCSSLayers ownership; see deferrals.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: versioning
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Additive fields only, sub-records at schemaVersion 1; ABI, manifest, artifacts and build-report schema versions unchanged; reader compatibility proven by execution.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: simulator evidence
orchestratorDecisions.decision: iOS Simulator evidence is labelled executed-simulator; Playwright WebKit never counts as Safari evidence.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: minimum target floor
orchestratorDecisions.decision: PandamStyle does not support pre-2022 engines. A resolved target below Chrome/Edge/Firefox 100 (and_chr and and_ff likewise), Safari/iOS Safari 15.4, Android WebView 100, or an Electron or Chromium-based browser (via the pinned baseline-browser-mapping Blink version) below Chromium 100 is refused with PMS_INVALID_TARGET_CONFIG (targets.below-minimum). The floors live in packages/compiler/src/targets/profiles/minimum.v1.json. A subfeature the pinned data marks native on every engine at the floor is classified below-floor by the data-derived guard (targets-subfeature-test.js), never by hand review. The default and built-in profiles are above the floor and unchanged.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: user-select transformation
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Accepted: user-select on safari and safari_ios is transformed-with-proof on compat-data proof plus Chrome-executed fixtures (evidence class E4 executed on chrome; E4 on safari and safari_ios deferred to #81). Every admitted user-select value is paired, so a descendant's explicit value overrides an ancestor's prefixed none even if WebKit inherits the prefixed form; whether WebKit inherits it is an open #81 check.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: alternative-value
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Re-deferred to CE-07.3 (#62).

orchestratorDecisions.subject: closure record
orchestratorDecisions.decision: No new file: CE-01.2 closures are appended to decision-closures.v1.json as one register; its AgentDoc evidence is repinned after re-review.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: default profile
orchestratorDecisions.decision: default.v1.json is regenerated by measure-floor.mjs without the user-select exception; the floors are unchanged.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: Next final asset
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Next is verified in CE-01.2 against the delivered CSS; superseded by CE-01.2-Q6 to Q8: under the declaration-equivalence contract a minification-only Next output passes and is not a known non-canonical mode, so no #78 deferral is recorded.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: host contract
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Declaration equivalence replaces byte identity for delivered host CSS; one shared normaliser built on a parser already in the dependency tree, with class tests (accepted: minified, comment-stripped, selector-list reordered; rejected: dropped -webkit- declaration, reordered declarations, merged rule, changed value). Hosts' own source maps are the host's concern.

orchestratorDecisions.subject: Rsbuild
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Fixed in CE-01.2 (a semantic AC3 violation): the stylesheet does not go through target-based lowering or prefix removal (lightningcss-loader, PostCSS, the browserslist-driven minimizer), whatever output.overrideBrowserslist says; fixture with overrideBrowserslist ['chrome >= 100'].

orchestratorDecisions.subject: Next
orchestratorDecisions.decision: Minification-only output is declaration-equivalent and passes; if Next altered declarations, the orchestrator is told before pushing.

deferrals.currentBehavior: the fallback kind is in the schema and refused with PMS_INVALID_ENHANCEMENT_POLICY (context.deferredTo CE-01.2)
prefixed-only data stays incompatible; user-select on safari and safari_ios is a non-binding exception of the default profile

deferrals.item: D-BP-09 transformation engine and identity stage
deferrals.currentBehavior: no transformation; transformed-with-proof is in the schema and never computed

deferrals.item: D-BP-10 layer lowering and useCSSLayers ownership
deferrals.currentBehavior: layers are native-only; useCSSLayers stays a host option

register.record: closures D-BP-01..13, orchestratorDecisions CE-01.1-O1..O13, deferrals, unknowns
closes D-BP-07, D-BP-09 and D-BP-10 (the CE-01.1 text is kept under supersedes), adds CE-01.2-T1..T3, orchestratorDecisions CE-01.2-Q1..Q8 and the resolution of each CE-01.1 deferral
